The limits that DO bind are: the documented AGGREGATE catalog ceiling of 10,000 tools with defer_loading (see max_total_tools), the documented selection cliff — Anthropic states "Claude's ability to pick the right tool degrades once you exceed 30-50 available tools" — the 1M/200k context window the serialized tool JSON is billed into, and the 32 MB request payload limit. Scope: aggregate (all connected MCP servers + built-in tools in one request), not per server.

max_tools_practical.notes: Anthropic documents the same 30-50 tool selection cliff for all models. 30 — the bottom of the documented band — is used for Haiku 4.5 because the 200k window is 5x smaller than the rest of the roster, so tool definitions cross a damaging share of the budget far sooner: Anthropic's own ~55k-token 5-server MCP example consumes 27.5% of Haiku's window versus 5.5% on a 1M model. EMPIRICAL, not an enforced spec value.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Tools are {name, description, input_schema} in the tools[] array; name must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$. Definitions are serialized into an API-injected tool-use system prompt. MCP tools arrive as mcp_toolset objects and are counted identically as input tokens.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool definitions are billed as input tokens, plus an injected tool-use system prompt: Claude Haiku 4.5 costs 496 tokens with tool_choice auto|none and 588 tokens with any|tool (re-read 2026-08-19). On a 200k window that fixed overhead is ~0.3% of the budget before a single tool definition is counted.

tool_search_deferral.notes: Listed in the tool search model-compatibility table with both tool_search_tool_regex_20251119 and tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119. Claude Code names Haiku 4.5 as one of the models that support tool_reference blocks. Deferral matters most on this model: the smallest window in the roster makes upfront tool definitions the dominant context cost.

max_tool_name_len.notes: "Must match the regex ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$." MCP client namespacing (server prefix + tool name) eats into this budget. Agent Skill names have a separate 64-character limit.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No character or token cap on tool description length is documented as of 2026-08-19. Anthropic's guidance is the opposite direction — "Aim for at least 3-4 sentences for each tool description, more if the tool is complex." Descriptions are billed as input tokens, so the binding ceilings are the context window and the 32 MB request payload limit.

max_request_size.notes: Direct Claude API: 32 MB for Messages and Token Counting (also Sessions/Agents/Environments); Message Batches API 256 MB; Files API 500 MB. Exceeding returns 413 request_too_large. Partner platforms differ: Amazon Bedrock 20 MB, Google Cloud 30 MB; Claude Platform on AWS uses the same limits as the direct API. Tool definitions count toward this payload AND toward the context window — two separate ceilings.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No per-tool-result byte or token cap is documented at the model-API layer; tool_result content blocks are billed as input tokens and are bounded by the 32 MB request limit and the context window. The documented cap that DOES bind sits at the client layer: Claude Code warns when an MCP tool result exceeds 10,000 tokens and truncates at 25,000 tokens by default (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS; a server may override per tool with the anthropic/maxResultSizeChars annotation). Programmatic tool calling is the other lever — results of tools called from inside the code-execution container do not enter the model's context at all.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel tool use is supported — an assistant turn can contain several tool_use blocks — but no numeric cap on simultaneous calls per turn is published. Bounded in practice by the turn's output-token budget. tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use:true forces at most one tool call per response (exactly one when tool_choice is any/tool).

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No per-turn tool-call-cycle cap is published in the Messages API docs. The controls that DO bound an agentic turn are: max_tokens (hard — truncates with stop_reason max_tokens), task budgets (beta, advisory soft hint, minimum 20,000 tokens, Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 only), and tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use, which restricts a turn to at most one tool call.

max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric cap on the mcp_servers array per request is documented for the MCP connector; the connector only requires that each mcp_server_name is referenced by exactly one mcp_toolset. At the client layer Claude Code states it "can connect to hundreds of external tools and data sources" and that it "doesn't impose a fixed per-server tool cap; the practical limit is your context window budget". The binding constraints are therefore the aggregate tool budget and the window, not a server count.

max_total_tools.notes: AGGREGATE ceiling across ALL connected MCP servers + built-in tools in one request (NOT a per-server cap), and conditional on tool search / defer_loading: "Maximum deferred tools: 10,000 tools with defer_loading: true per request". Without defer_loading the binding constraint is the documented 30-50 tool selection cliff plus the context window. Anthropic's own example: a 5-server setup (GitHub, Slack, Sentry, Grafana, Splunk) costs ~55k tokens in definitions before any work; tool search cuts that by over 85%.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Tools are {name, description, input_schema (JSON Schema)} with optional input_examples, cache_control, strict, defer_loading, allowed_callers and eager_input_streaming. Structured outputs / strict tool use share one documented JSON Schema restriction: pattern (regex) is NOT supported — the Python, TypeScript, Ruby and PHP SDKs strip unsupported keywords and fold them into field descriptions. No documented maximum nesting depth, maximum property count, maximum enum size or maximum total schema size. strict is available on all tools except mcp_toolset; defer_loading is available on all tools (per-tool or per-toolset for MCP). input_examples cost ~20-50 tokens for simple examples and ~100-200 tokens for complex nested objects, and are not available on server tools. Tool definitions can carry cache_control, so a repeated tool array reads at 0.1x input price after a cache write; deferred tools sit outside the system-prompt prefix so defer_loading preserves the cached prefix and composes with strict mode without grammar recompilation. On a 200k window tool definitions are proportionally 5x more expensive than on the 1M models, so defer_loading plus cache_control on the tools array is close to mandatory for multi-server MCP setups. Note the 4,096-token minimum cacheable prompt on this model — small tool arrays may not be cacheable at all.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: MCP connector (API layer, beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20; mcp-client-2025-04-04 is deprecated): HTTPS remote servers only over Streamable HTTP or SSE — local stdio servers cannot be attached directly. Of the MCP specification only tool calls are supported; prompts and resources are not. Available on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (Hosted-on-Anthropic deployments), all in beta. Per-tool mcp_toolset config exposes enabled and defer_loading (default false). Tool search regex variant: max 200-character pattern; error_code values are invalid_tool_input, unavailable, too_many_requests and execution_time_exceeded. Request size 32 MB direct / 20 MB Bedrock / 30 MB Google Cloud. A single request may carry up to 600 images or PDF pages on 1M-window models (100 on 200k-window models). Haiku 4.5 supports tool search / defer_loading, structured outputs / strict tool use, the memory tool, and the automatic context-awareness signals (<budget:token_budget> plus a per-tool-call <system_warning> usage line). It does NOT support task budgets (beta) and is NOT in the programmatic tool calling support list (which requires code_execution_20260120 and covers Fable 5, Mythos 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6/4.5, Sonnet 5/4.6/4.5) — so the ~38% billed-input saving from keeping tool results out of context is unavailable here, which makes defer_loading and client-side result trimming the only levers. A 200k-window model accepts at most 100 images or PDF pages per request (600 on 1M models). Haiku 4.5 supports extended thinking but not adaptive thinking.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop / 5-depth / no-oneOf. Anthropic does ship a strict flag (strict:true, plus structured outputs) but its documented rule set is different and looser: the only keyword restriction published is that pattern (regex) is unsupported, and no property-count or depth ceiling is given. Captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.

skills_supported.notes: Agent Skills available on the Claude API, claude.ai, Claude Code (custom Skills only), Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (pre-built Skills require a Hosted-on-Anthropic deployment).

skills_loading_model.notes: Level 1 metadata (name + description from YAML frontmatter, ~100 tokens per Skill) is always in context at startup. Level 2 (SKILL.md body, under 5k tokens) loads only when the Skill triggers. Level 3+ bundled files load only when read; scripts run through bash so only their output enters context. Documented field limits: name max 64 characters (lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens; no XML tags; may not contain "anthropic" or "claude"), description non-empty and max 1024 characters.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: ~100 tokens per installed Skill at startup (Level 1 name+description). When a Skill triggers, its SKILL.md body adds under 5k tokens (Level 2). Level 3 bundled files cost nothing until read; scripts execute through bash so only stdout/stderr enters context. Anthropic states you "can install many Skills without context penalty: until a Skill is triggered, only its name and description occupy context", and documents no numeric ceiling on the number of installed Skills; the binding limit is the context window -- each installed Skill holds its name and description in context, and its full instructions load on invocation.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: Tool-use system prompt overhead: 496 tokens (tool_choice auto/none) or 588 tokens (any/tool). Context awareness is active. Note the 4,096-token minimum cacheable prompt length — the highest in the current roster (Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Mythos 5 need only 512) — so short tool arrays and short Skill sets may fall below the caching threshold entirely. System-added tokens are counted but not billed.

prompt_caching.notes: Supported on all active Claude models, automatic and explicit. Multipliers: 5-minute cache write 1.25x base input, 1-hour cache write 2x, cache read (hit) 0.1x. For Claude Haiku 4.5 that is $1.25/MTok (5m write), $2.0/MTok (1h write) and $0.1/MTok (read) against a $1.0/MTok base. Minimum cacheable prompt length: 4,096 tokens. cache_control can be set on tool definitions and on an mcp_toolset, so a stable MCP tool array is cacheable; deferred tools sit outside the cached system-prompt prefix and do not invalidate it.

memory_feature.notes: First-party memory tool (memory_20250818), generally available on the Messages API with no beta header, on "all Claude 4 and later models". Operates as just-in-time retrieval: Claude checks its memory directory and reads files back on demand, so retrieved content enters the window as ordinary input tokens rather than a permanent always-on block. Anthropic does not publish a token accounting rule for memory content.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cache read (hit) = 0.1x base input. 5-minute cache write = 1.25x, 1-hour cache write = 2x.

batch_discount.notes: Message Batches API: $0.5/MTok input, $2.5/MTok output for Claude Haiku 4.5. Batch and prompt-caching discounts stack, and both apply at standard rates across the full context window.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Images billed as input tokens at the STANDARD visual-token rate (max 1568 tokens/image); Anthropic's example puts a 1000x1000 image at about $1.30 per thousand images on Haiku 4.5. PDFs the same; audio unsupported. At most 100 images or PDF pages per request on a 200k-window model.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Thinking tokens count toward the context window, count toward rate limits, are a subset of max_tokens, and are billed at the output rate ($5.0/MTok here).

release_date.notes: Announcement page: "October 15, 2025", "$1/$5 per million input and output tokens", "available everywhere today" (Claude Code, web apps, Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI). Corroborated by the deprecation table's tentative retirement "not sooner than October 15, 2026". Re-verified 2026-08-19.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Latest models comparison table (re-read 2026-08-19): reliable knowledge cutoff Feb 2025, training data cutoff Jul 2025 — by far the oldest cutoff in the current roster.

detail.notes: Claude Haiku 4.5 (2025-10-15) is unchanged at this refresh and remains Anthropic's fastest, cheapest model — and the only current model with a 200k rather than 1M window, which makes MCP tool-footprint management the binding constraint. WATCH: the deprecations table gives a tentative retirement "not sooner than October 15, 2026", the nearest retirement horizon of any active Claude model, and there is no Haiku 5 as of 2026-08-19. Uses the previous (pre-4.7) tokenizer, so token counts are NOT comparable with Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Fable 5 measurements. Strips previous-turn thinking blocks. Supports extended thinking, not adaptive thinking. API model ID claude-haiku-4-5 (alias) or claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (pinned snapshot).

context_window_tokens.notes: Model page: 'Input token limit: 1,048,576'; DeepMind model card: 'a token context window of up to 1M'.

input_output_shared.notes: CHANGED from the 2026-06-21 revision, which asserted a single shared pool. Google publishes two separate rows -- 'Input token limit: 1,048,576' and 'Output token limit: 65,536' -- and nowhere documents output drawing down the input budget; the Gemini 3 guide likewise says '1 million token input context window and up to 64k tokens of output'. Recorded as not-shared with medium confidence because Google never states the relationship explicitly either way.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Google documents a single output limit, not a default/max pair.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Model page: 'Output token limit: 65,536'; model card: '64K token output'.

extended_context.notes: 1,048,576 is the standard GA input window; no beta or extended window is offered.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Thinking tokens are reported in the usage payload as total_thought_tokens and billed at the output rate. thinking_level (low / medium (default) / high) replaces the removed thinking_budget parameter.

tokenizer_family.notes: Proprietary Gemini tokenizer (closed). Docs: 'For Gemini models, a token is equivalent to about 4 characters. 100 tokens is equal to about 60-80 English words.'

tokenizer_public.notes: Vocabulary/weights are not published; exact counts require the countTokens API.

tokenizer_access.notes: client.models.count_tokens() (Python/JS) or the REST models.countTokens endpoint. Counting the full request -- including the tools array -- is the only exact way to measure an MCP server's definition footprint.

count_tokens_method.value: client.models.count_tokens(model='gemini-3.7-flash', contents=...) — Python SDK; ai.models.countTokens({model:'gemini-3.7-flash', contents:...}) — JS SDK; or POST /v1beta/models/gemini-3.7-flash:countTokens

image_token_rule.value: Images with both dimensions <=384 pixels = 258 tokens. Larger images are tiled into 768x768 pixel tiles, each tile = 258 tokens.
image_token_rule.notes: Gemini 3 models expose media_resolution to cap tokens per image/frame; the Gemini 3 guide warns that higher default resolutions can push requests over the context window.

audio_token_rule.notes: Video converts at 263 tokens per second.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Docs: 'a token is equivalent to about 4 characters'.

function_calling.notes: Model page lists Function calling as supported.

native_mcp.notes: RE-SOURCED 2026-08-19. The previous citation was the Antigravity agent page, which documents MCP only for that managed agent; this source_url is the Gemini API function-calling documentation itself, which defines a first-class 'mcp_server' tool type (type/name/url, optional headers and allowed_tools) and states 'Interactions API supports connecting to remote MCP servers to give the model access to external tools and services' -- and gemini-3.7-flash is the model used in every remote-MCP example on that page (Python, JavaScript and REST). SCOPE AND CAVEATS: (a) transport is restricted -- 'Remote MCP only works with Streamable HTTP servers. SSE (Server-Sent Events) servers are not supported'; (b) 'MCP server names should not include the - character. Use snake_case server names instead'; (c) the Interactions API overview page still carries the contradicting limitation 'Gemini 3 does not support remote MCP, this is coming soon' (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions-overview) -- vendor docs conflict, hence medium confidence; (d) plain generateContent has no server-side MCP tool type: client-side MCP goes through the google-genai SDK's MCP client, which its docs still label 'Built-in MCP support is an experimental feature' (https://googleapis.github.io/python-genai/); (e) the Antigravity managed agent (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/antigravity-agent) is a separate product surface where remote MCP servers are registered server-side, and is not evidence for the model API. MCP tools only -- resources and prompts are not consumed.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Verbatim: 'The model supports calling multiple functions in a single turn (parallel function calling)' and 'in sequence (compositional function calling)'.

max_tools_hard.notes: TIER 4 / OBSERVED API ERROR, NOT PUBLISHED SPEC (re-graded 2026-08-19 from tier 2 -- a GitHub issue is tier 4 under methodology section 4 even when it quotes a real API rejection). The cited Gemini CLI issue (opened 2026-02-14, closed 'not planned') reports the verbatim API rejection 'At most 512 function declarations can be specified' when many MCP servers are enabled. UNCONFIRMED BY VENDOR DOCS: on 2026-08-19 I opened the Gemini API function-calling docs (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling -- no numeric cap, only the best practice 'Keep active set to 10-20 tools maximum'), the Interactions API overview (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions-overview), the Live API tools page (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/tools), the Vertex REST FunctionDeclaration reference and the Gemini Enterprise / Vertex function-calling reference; none of them publishes a maximum number of function declarations. The only tier-1 count Google publishes sits on a DIFFERENT surface: Firebase AI Logic states 'The maximum number of function declarations that you can provide with the request is 128' (https://firebase.google.com/docs/ai-logic/function-calling), presented there as a Firebase AI Logic SDK constraint. Planning guidance: 128 is the conservative documented number on that SDK; 512 is the observed hard rejection point on the raw API. SCOPE: aggregate -- summed across every connected MCP server plus built-in tools in one request; there is no per-MCP-server cap.

max_tools_practical.notes: Google's own function-calling best practices state: 'Tool Selection: Keep active set to 10-20 tools maximum.' Recorded at the top of that band (20). This is vendor ADVICE, not an enforced cap and not a measured cliff, hence medium confidence. Searched for Gemini-specific empirical tool-count degradation data and found none: the most recent public study (Superhuman, June 2026, 584-tool / 110-agent catalog, flat-routing F1 58.2% at 51 tools falling to 42.1% at 584) tested GPT-5.4, GPT-5.1 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 only -- no Google models. The limits that DO bind for Gemini: this ~10-20 advisory band, the 512 aggregate declaration ceiling (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard), and the 1,048,576-token input window.

tool_definition_shape.notes: functionDeclarations[] inside a Tool object: {name, description, parameters (OpenAPI/JSON-Schema subset)}. The Interactions API additionally accepts a tool of type 'mcp_server' {name, url, headers, allowed_tools} that is expanded server-side rather than serialized by the caller.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool/function declarations are serialized into the request and billed as input tokens. Since the 2026 token-accounting update the usage payload breaks them out as total_tool_use_tokens, so the definition footprint can be measured directly instead of inferred.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No deferred/lazy tool loading at the model-API layer -- there is no Gemini analogue of Anthropic's tool-search / defer_loading. Two partial mitigations exist and are NOT the same thing: (a) the Interactions API mcp_server tool takes an allowed_tools allowlist, a static pre-filter applied before definitions reach the model; (b) implicit/explicit context caching amortizes a static tool block. Gemini CLI's Agent Skills do use progressive disclosure, but that defers SKILL.md bodies, not tool definitions.

max_tool_name_len.notes: RE-SOURCED 2026-08-19 to Google's own FunctionDeclaration reference (the previous citation was an unrelated third-party repo issue, tier 4). Firebase's FunctionDeclaration reference states verbatim: 'The name of the function to call. Must start with a letter or an underscore. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a max length of 64.' Google's Vertex AI REST FunctionDeclaration reference carries the same constraint with dots also allowed: 'Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores, dots and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.' SCOPE: per-tool, API-enforced. This bites MCP servers because hosts namespace tool names -- Gemini CLI prefixes every MCP tool as mcp_{serverName}_{toolName} and truncates names over 63 characters, so a long server name silently eats the 64-character budget.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented character or token cap on function/tool description strings; re-checked 2026-08-19 against the function-calling page and the Interactions API reference, which document description as an untyped optional string. The effective constraints are the 1,048,576-token input window and the undocumented 'very large or deeply nested schemas' rejection.

max_request_size.notes: Verbatim: inline data '100 MB per request or payload' with '50 MB for PDFs'; external/signed URLs '100 MB per request/payload'. Larger payloads go through the Files API ('2 GB per file, up to 20GB per project', retained '48 Hours'). This is the HTTP payload ceiling; for text + tool-definition traffic the 1,048,576-token input limit binds first.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-functionResponse size cap in bytes or tokens. Gemini 3 models accept multimodal function responses (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain inline in the response part) and require each response to carry a matching call_id and name. Tool results consume the same 1,048,576-token input budget as everything else.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel function calling is supported with no documented numeric cap on how many calls may be emitted in one turn. Gemini 3 returns a unique id per function call and requires exactly one response per call, matched by id and name -- results may return out of order but must be 1:1.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.unit: automatic function-calling remote calls per request (SDK default)
tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: CHANGED from null. SCOPE: SDK layer, not the model API. The google-genai SDK's automatic function calling loops with a default maximum of 10 remote calls per request; it is configurable and can be disabled, after which the caller drives the loop. The Gemini API itself documents no per-turn numeric cap on tool-call/result cycles -- there is no 'reached its tool-use limit' error analogous to Claude's, so the limits that actually bind a long agentic run are the 512-declaration aggregate ceiling (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard) and the 1,048,576-token input window. The Interactions API does not support Python automatic function calling at all. Source re-pointed 2026-08-19 from the googleapis/python-genai GitHub repo to Google's published SDK documentation site, which states verbatim: 'by default the SDK will perform automatic function calling until the remote calls exceed the maximum remote call for automatic function calling (default to 10 times)'.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented cap on simultaneous MCP server connections at the API layer, and the Interactions API reference documents no numeric cap on how many mcp_server tools an interaction may carry. The binding constraint is the 512 aggregate functionDeclarations (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard). Client layer for contrast: Gemini CLI users report tools being 'silently dropped' past roughly 100 aggregate MCP tools (https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21823, closed), and Gemini CLI's docs set a 600,000 ms (10 minute) default per-server request timeout.

max_total_tools.notes: TIER 4 / OBSERVED API ERROR, NOT PUBLISHED SPEC (re-graded 2026-08-19 from tier 2 -- a GitHub issue is tier 4 under methodology section 4 even when it quotes a real API rejection). The cited Gemini CLI issue (opened 2026-02-14, closed 'not planned') reports the verbatim API rejection 'At most 512 function declarations can be specified' when many MCP servers are enabled. UNCONFIRMED BY VENDOR DOCS: on 2026-08-19 I opened the Gemini API function-calling docs (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling -- no numeric cap, only the best practice 'Keep active set to 10-20 tools maximum'), the Interactions API overview (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions-overview), the Live API tools page (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/tools), the Vertex REST FunctionDeclaration reference and the Gemini Enterprise / Vertex function-calling reference; none of them publishes a maximum number of function declarations. The only tier-1 count Google publishes sits on a DIFFERENT surface: Firebase AI Logic states 'The maximum number of function declarations that you can provide with the request is 128' (https://firebase.google.com/docs/ai-logic/function-calling), presented there as a Firebase AI Logic SDK constraint. Planning guidance: 128 is the conservative documented number on that SDK; 512 is the observed hard rejection point on the raw API. SCOPE: aggregate client/API ceiling, identical in substance to max_tools_hard -- summed across every connected MCP server plus built-in tools in one request; there is no per-MCP-server cap.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Only a subset of the OpenAPI schema is accepted for function parameters (verbatim: 'Only a subset of the OpenAPI schema is supported'). Gemini 3-series and 2.5-series models accept type, nullable, required, format, description, properties, items, enum, anyOf, $ref, minItems, maxItems, minimum, maximum. Documented soft constraint, verbatim: 'For any mode, the API may reject very large or deeply nested schemas' -- Google publishes no numeric nesting-depth or property-count cap, so there is nothing analogous to OpenAI strict mode's 100-property / 5-level rules. Function names are validated by the API against 'Must start with a letter or an underscore. Must be alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), underscores (_), dots (.), colons (:), or dashes (-), with a maximum length of 64.' For MCP the function-calling page adds: 'MCP server names should not include the - character. Use snake_case server names instead.' Sources: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling , https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode/issues/235
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: RATE LIMITS: Google no longer publishes per-model RPM/TPM/RPD tables -- the rate-limits page now says limits 'can be viewed in Google AI Studio' (only Batch API enqueued-token quotas remain tabulated), so the per-model rate numbers carried in the 2026-06-21 revision of this dataset are no longer sourceable and have been removed rather than restated. API CHANGES since 2026-06-21: the Interactions API went GA in June 2026 and is now the recommended surface for all new projects; the sampling parameters temperature / top_p / top_k were deprecated 2026-07-21; thinking_budget is replaced by thinking_level. The Interactions API does NOT support explicit context caching (implicit only, via previous_interaction_id), the Batch API, or Python automatic function calling. Tool configuration is interaction-scoped and must be re-sent on every interaction, so tool-definition tokens are re-paid per interaction unless implicit caching hits. Token accounting now exposes total_tool_use_tokens, total_thought_tokens and total_cached_tokens in the usage payload -- total_tool_use_tokens makes an MCP server's definition footprint directly measurable. MODEL-SPECIFIC: 3.7 Flash is on introductory pricing through 2026-12-31 and doubles on 2027-01-01, so any tool-heavy cost model must carry that step. It is also the default model of the Antigravity managed agent, the only surface with server-side remote MCP today. Minimum cacheable prompt 4,096 tokens.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode. Gemini enforces its own looser OpenAPI-subset keyword rules plus an undocumented size/nesting rejection -- captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.

skills_supported.notes: CHANGED from false. Google now ships Agent Skills: a SKILL.md-based, model-invokable instruction bundle with an official library (github.com/google-gemini/gemini-skills, Apache-2.0), publicised 2026-03-25 and documented on ai.google.dev. IMPORTANT SCOPE: skills live at the AGENT/CLI layer (Gemini CLI, Antigravity, third-party coding assistants), not in the model API -- the Gemini docs state 'Most agents index skills only on startup' and the generateContent / Interactions endpoints neither accept nor process a skill object. For a raw API caller the only always-on instruction channel is still system_instruction, and Gems remain a consumer-product feature.

skills_loading_model.notes: Verbatim (Gemini CLI): 'At the start of a session, Gemini CLI scans the discovery tiers and injects the name and description of all enabled skills into the system prompt' and 'Only skill metadata (name and description) is loaded initially. Detailed instructions and resources are only disclosed when the model explicitly activates the skill, saving context tokens.' Activation is itself a tool call (activate_skill), after which 'The SKILL.md body and folder structure is added to the conversation history'.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Skills never enter a Gemini API request as a first-class object -- the agent host injects skill name+description into the system prompt at session start and appends the SKILL.md body only after activate_skill fires. The resident cost is therefore one metadata line per enabled skill and the burst cost is the skill body, both billed as ordinary input tokens. System instructions are billed as input on every request; caching can absorb a static instruction + tool-definition prefix once it clears the model's minimum cacheable size.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System instructions are counted as part of the input tokens; Google documents no fixed per-request overhead beyond the caller-supplied content. native_mcp.notes: RE-SOURCED 2026-08-19 to Google's published google-genai SDK documentation, which states 'Built-in MCP support is an experimental feature' and shows a local MCP ClientSession passed straight into tools=[session] with automatic function calling (example model: gemini-2.5-flash). That CLIENT-SIDE path is what makes native_mcp true for this model. The previously cited Interactions API overview does NOT support the claim for this model -- its limitations section says 'Gemini 3 does not support remote MCP, this is coming soon' (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions-overview). The server-side 'mcp_server' tool type documented on https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling is exercised there only with gemini-3.7-flash, and remote MCP is Streamable-HTTP only ('SSE (Server-Sent Events) servers are not supported'). MCP tools only -- resources and prompts are not consumed. Confidence medium: the supported path is an SDK feature the vendor labels experimental, and the two vendor pages conflict on remote MCP.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Verbatim: 'The model supports calling multiple functions in a single turn (parallel function calling)' and 'in sequence (compositional function calling)'.

max_tools_hard.notes: TIER 4 / OBSERVED API ERROR, NOT PUBLISHED SPEC (re-graded 2026-08-19 from tier 2 -- a GitHub issue is tier 4 under methodology section 4 even when it quotes a real API rejection). The cited Gemini CLI issue (opened 2026-02-14, closed 'not planned') reports the verbatim API rejection 'At most 512 function declarations can be specified' when many MCP servers are enabled. UNCONFIRMED BY VENDOR DOCS: on 2026-08-19 I opened the Gemini API function-calling docs (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling -- no numeric cap, only the best practice 'Keep active set to 10-20 tools maximum'), the Interactions API overview (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions-overview), the Live API tools page (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/tools), the Vertex REST FunctionDeclaration reference and the Gemini Enterprise / Vertex function-calling reference; none of them publishes a maximum number of function declarations. The only tier-1 count Google publishes sits on a DIFFERENT surface: Firebase AI Logic states 'The maximum number of function declarations that you can provide with the request is 128' (https://firebase.google.com/docs/ai-logic/function-calling), presented there as a Firebase AI Logic SDK constraint. Planning guidance: 128 is the conservative documented number on that SDK; 512 is the observed hard rejection point on the raw API. SCOPE: aggregate -- summed across every connected MCP server plus built-in tools in one request; there is no per-MCP-server cap.

max_tools_practical.notes: Google's own function-calling best practices state: 'Tool Selection: Keep active set to 10-20 tools maximum.' Recorded at the top of that band (20). This is vendor ADVICE, not an enforced cap and not a measured cliff, hence medium confidence. Searched for Gemini-specific empirical tool-count degradation data and found none: the most recent public study (Superhuman, June 2026, 584-tool / 110-agent catalog, flat-routing F1 58.2% at 51 tools falling to 42.1% at 584) tested GPT-5.4, GPT-5.1 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 only -- no Google models. The limits that DO bind for Gemini: this ~10-20 advisory band, the 512 aggregate declaration ceiling (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard), and the 1,048,576-token input window.

tool_definition_shape.notes: functionDeclarations[] inside a Tool object: {name, description, parameters (OpenAPI/JSON-Schema subset)}. The Interactions API additionally accepts a tool of type 'mcp_server' {name, url, headers, allowed_tools} that is expanded server-side rather than serialized by the caller.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool/function declarations are serialized into the request and billed as input tokens. Since the 2026 token-accounting update the usage payload breaks them out as total_tool_use_tokens, so the definition footprint can be measured directly instead of inferred.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No deferred/lazy tool loading at the model-API layer -- there is no Gemini analogue of Anthropic's tool-search / defer_loading. Two partial mitigations exist and are NOT the same thing: (a) the Interactions API mcp_server tool takes an allowed_tools allowlist, a static pre-filter applied before definitions reach the model; (b) implicit/explicit context caching amortizes a static tool block. Gemini CLI's Agent Skills do use progressive disclosure, but that defers SKILL.md bodies, not tool definitions.

max_tool_name_len.notes: RE-SOURCED 2026-08-19 to Google's own FunctionDeclaration reference (the previous citation was an unrelated third-party repo issue, tier 4). Firebase's FunctionDeclaration reference states verbatim: 'The name of the function to call. Must start with a letter or an underscore. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a max length of 64.' Google's Vertex AI REST FunctionDeclaration reference carries the same constraint with dots also allowed: 'Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores, dots and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.' SCOPE: per-tool, API-enforced. This bites MCP servers because hosts namespace tool names -- Gemini CLI prefixes every MCP tool as mcp_{serverName}_{toolName} and truncates names over 63 characters, so a long server name silently eats the 64-character budget.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented character or token cap on function/tool description strings; re-checked 2026-08-19 against the function-calling page and the Interactions API reference, which document description as an untyped optional string. The effective constraints are the 1,048,576-token input window and the undocumented 'very large or deeply nested schemas' rejection.

max_request_size.notes: Verbatim: inline data '100 MB per request or payload' with '50 MB for PDFs'; external/signed URLs '100 MB per request/payload'. Larger payloads go through the Files API ('2 GB per file, up to 20GB per project', retained '48 Hours'). This is the HTTP payload ceiling; for text + tool-definition traffic the 1,048,576-token input limit binds first.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-functionResponse size cap in bytes or tokens. Gemini 3 models accept multimodal function responses (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain inline in the response part) and require each response to carry a matching call_id and name. Tool results consume the same 1,048,576-token input budget as everything else.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel function calling is supported with no documented numeric cap on how many calls may be emitted in one turn. Gemini 3 returns a unique id per function call and requires exactly one response per call, matched by id and name -- results may return out of order but must be 1:1.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.unit: automatic function-calling remote calls per request (SDK default)
tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: CHANGED from null. SCOPE: SDK layer, not the model API. The google-genai SDK's automatic function calling loops with a default maximum of 10 remote calls per request; it is configurable and can be disabled, after which the caller drives the loop. The Gemini API itself documents no per-turn numeric cap on tool-call/result cycles -- there is no 'reached its tool-use limit' error analogous to Claude's, so the limits that actually bind a long agentic run are the 512-declaration aggregate ceiling (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard) and the 1,048,576-token input window. The binding constraint is the 512 aggregate functionDeclarations (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard). Client layer for contrast: Gemini CLI users report tools being 'silently dropped' past roughly 100 aggregate MCP tools (https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21823, closed), and Gemini CLI's docs set a 600,000 ms (10 minute) default per-server request timeout.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Only a subset of the OpenAPI schema is accepted for function parameters (verbatim: 'Only a subset of the OpenAPI schema is supported'). Gemini 3-series and 2.5-series models accept type, nullable, required, format, description, properties, items, enum, anyOf, $ref, minItems, maxItems, minimum, maximum. Documented soft constraint, verbatim: 'For any mode, the API may reject very large or deeply nested schemas' -- Google publishes no numeric nesting-depth or property-count cap, so there is nothing analogous to OpenAI strict mode's 100-property / 5-level rules. Function names are validated by the API against 'Must start with a letter or an underscore. Must be alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), underscores (_), dots (.), colons (:), or dashes (-), with a maximum length of 64.' For MCP the function-calling page adds: 'MCP server names should not include the - character. Use snake_case server names instead.' Sources: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling , https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode/issues/235
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: RATE LIMITS: Google no longer publishes per-model RPM/TPM/RPD tables -- the rate-limits page now says limits 'can be viewed in Google AI Studio' (only Batch API enqueued-token quotas remain tabulated), so the per-model rate numbers carried in the 2026-06-21 revision of this dataset are no longer sourceable and have been removed rather than restated. API CHANGES since 2026-06-21: the Interactions API went GA in June 2026 and is now the recommended surface for all new projects; the sampling parameters temperature / top_p / top_k were deprecated 2026-07-21; thinking_budget is replaced by thinking_level. The Interactions API does NOT support explicit context caching (implicit only, via previous_interaction_id), the Batch API, or Python automatic function calling. Tool configuration is interaction-scoped and must be re-sent on every interaction, so tool-definition tokens are re-paid per interaction unless implicit caching hits. Token accounting now exposes total_tool_use_tokens, total_thought_tokens and total_cached_tokens in the usage payload -- total_tool_use_tokens makes an MCP server's definition footprint directly measurable. MODEL-SPECIFIC: 3.6 Flash carries the same introductory price card as 3.7 Flash through 2026-12-31 and doubles on 2027-01-01. Minimum cacheable prompt 4,096 tokens.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode. Gemini enforces its own looser OpenAPI-subset keyword rules plus an undocumented size/nesting rejection -- captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.

skills_supported.notes: CHANGED from false. Google now ships Agent Skills: a SKILL.md-based, model-invokable instruction bundle with an official library (github.com/google-gemini/gemini-skills, Apache-2.0), publicised 2026-03-25 and documented on ai.google.dev. skills_loading_model.notes: Verbatim (Gemini CLI): 'At the start of a session, Gemini CLI scans the discovery tiers and injects the name and description of all enabled skills into the system prompt' and 'Only skill metadata (name and description) is loaded initially. Activation is itself a tool call (activate_skill), after which 'The SKILL.md body and folder structure is added to the conversation history'.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Skills never enter a Gemini API request as a first-class object -- the agent host injects skill name+description into the system prompt at session start and appends the SKILL.md body only after activate_skill fires. max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented character or token cap on function/tool description strings; re-checked 2026-08-19 against the function-calling page and the Interactions API reference, which document description as an untyped optional string. The effective constraints are the 1,048,576-token input window and the undocumented 'very large or deeply nested schemas' rejection.

max_request_size.notes: Verbatim: inline data '100 MB per request or payload' with '50 MB for PDFs'; external/signed URLs '100 MB per request/payload'. Larger payloads go through the Files API ('2 GB per file, up to 20GB per project', retained '48 Hours'). This is the HTTP payload ceiling; for text + tool-definition traffic the 1,048,576-token input limit binds first.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel function calling is supported with no documented numeric cap on how many calls may be emitted in one turn. Gemini 3 returns a unique id per function call and requires exactly one response per call, matched by id and name -- results may return out of order but must be 1:1.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.unit: automatic function-calling remote calls per request (SDK default)

Function names are validated by the API against 'Must start with a letter or an underscore. Must be alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), underscores (_), dots (.), colons (:), or dashes (-), with a maximum length of 64.' skills_supported.notes: CHANGED from false. Google now ships Agent Skills: a SKILL.md-based, model-invokable instruction bundle with an official library (github.com/google-gemini/gemini-skills, Apache-2.0), publicised 2026-03-25 and documented on ai.google.dev. For a raw API caller the only always-on instruction channel is still system_instruction, and Gems remain a consumer-product feature.

skills_loading_model.notes: Verbatim (Gemini CLI): 'At the start of a session, Gemini CLI scans the discovery tiers and injects the name and description of all enabled skills into the system prompt' and 'Only skill metadata (name and description) is loaded initially. Detailed instructions and resources are only disclosed when the model explicitly activates the skill, saving context tokens.' Activation is itself a tool call (activate_skill), after which 'The SKILL.md body and folder structure is added to the conversation history'.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Skills never enter a Gemini API request as a first-class object -- the agent host injects skill name+description into the system prompt at session start and appends the SKILL.md body only after activate_skill fires. The resident cost is therefore one metadata line per enabled skill and the burst cost is the skill body, both billed as ordinary input tokens. System instructions are billed as input on every request; caching can absorb a static instruction + tool-definition prefix once it clears the model's minimum cacheable size.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System instructions are counted as part of the input tokens; Google documents no fixed per-request overhead beyond the caller-supplied content. In the Interactions API tools and system instructions are interaction-scoped and must be re-specified on every interaction, so a large MCP tool block is re-billed each turn unless implicit caching hits.

prompt_caching.notes: Implicit caching is enabled by default for all Gemini 2.5 and newer models; cache hits are reported in usage.total_cached_tokens. Minimum cacheable prompt for Gemini 3.7 / 3.6 / 3.5 Flash: 4,096 tokens (2,048 for Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro), so a small MCP tool block will not be cached at all. Explicit (manually created) caches work on generateContent but are NOT supported in the Interactions API. Cached read $0.15/1M; storage $1.00/1M tokens/hour.

memory_feature.notes: No persistent cross-session memory product in the Gemini Developer API. The closest primitive is the Interactions API's server-side conversation state via previous_interaction_id, which is per-conversation session state (and a caching optimization), not a durable memory store.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Re-verified unchanged. Standard paid tier; the pricing page lists no separate audio rate and no long-context tier for this model. Note it is now more expensive than the newer 3.7/3.6 Flash ($0.75 introductory).

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Re-verified unchanged. Includes thinking tokens.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Re-verified unchanged. Cache storage $1.00/1M tokens/hour.

batch_discount.value: 50% off standard price (Batch API: input $0.75/1M, output $4.50/1M)
batch_discount.notes: Re-verified unchanged.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: The pricing page lists no separate audio input rate for 3.5 Flash. Conversions: image 258 tokens per <=384px image or per 768x768 tile; audio 32 tokens/sec; video 263 tokens/sec. Search/Maps grounding billed separately (5,000 free requests/month, then $14 per 1,000).

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Thinking tokens billed at the output rate.

release_date.notes: Re-verified: the model-versions table lists gemini-3.5-flash release date 'May 19, 2026'; the model page still shows 'Latest update: May 2026'; the DeepMind model card says 'Published 19 May 2026'. Value unchanged, source refreshed to a page that currently states it.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Re-verified. The model page dropped its knowledge-cutoff row, but the 'What's new in Gemini 3.5 Flash' page still states 'January 2025'. Value unchanged, source_url moved to the page that currently states it.

detail.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19: still GA, no deprecation or shutdown date. It is no longer the flagship -- Gemini 3.6 Flash (2026-07-21) and 3.7 Flash (2026-08-13) both shipped since the last revision at half the introductory price with the same 1M/64k envelope, so 3.5 Flash is now the expensive middle of the Flash line. context_window_tokens.notes: Model page: 'Input token limit: 1,048,576'; DeepMind model card: 'a token context window of up to 1M'.

input_output_shared.notes: CHANGED from the 2026-06-21 revision, which asserted a single shared pool. max_output_tokens_default.notes: Google documents a single output limit, not a default/max pair.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Model page: 'Output token limit: 65,536'; model card: '64K token output'.

extended_context.notes: 1,048,576 is the standard GA input window; no beta or extended window is offered.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Thinking tokens are reported in the usage payload as total_thought_tokens and billed at the output rate. thinking_level (low / medium (default) / high) replaces the removed thinking_budget parameter.

tokenizer_family.notes: Proprietary Gemini tokenizer (closed). Docs: 'For Gemini models, a token is equivalent to about 4 characters. 100 tokens is equal to about 60-80 English words.'

tokenizer_public.notes: Vocabulary/weights are not published; exact counts require the countTokens API.

tokenizer_access.notes: client.models.count_tokens() (Python/JS) or the REST models.countTokens endpoint. Counting the full request -- including the tools array -- is the only exact way to measure an MCP server's definition footprint.

count_tokens_method.value: client.models.count_tokens(model='gemini-3.5-flash-lite', contents=...) — Python SDK; ai.models.countTokens({model:'gemini-3.5-flash-lite', contents:...}) — JS SDK; or POST /v1beta/models/gemini-3.5-flash-lite:countTokens

image_token_rule.value: Images with both dimensions <=384 pixels = 258 tokens. Larger images are tiled into 768x768 pixel tiles, each tile = 258 tokens.
image_token_rule.notes: Gemini 3 models expose media_resolution to cap tokens per image/frame; the Gemini 3 guide warns that higher default resolutions can push requests over the context window.

audio_token_rule.notes: Video converts at 263 tokens per second.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Docs: 'a token is equivalent to about 4 characters'.

function_calling.notes: Model page lists Function calling as supported.

The caching page's minimum-cacheable-prompt table lists Gemini 3.7/3.6/3.5 Flash (4,096) and Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro (2,048) but no Flash-Lite row, so the minimum for this model is undocumented. Explicit caches are not supported in the Interactions API.

memory_feature.notes: No persistent cross-session memory product in the Gemini Developer API. The closest primitive is the Interactions API's server-side conversation state via previous_interaction_id, which is per-conversation session state (and a caching optimization), not a durable memory store.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard paid tier. Free tier available. The pricing card lists no separate audio rate for this model (unlike 3.1 Flash-Lite, which charges $0.50/1M for audio).

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard paid tier; includes thinking tokens.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard-tier context caching read price; batch $0.02/1M, priority $0.05/1M. Cache storage $1.00/1M tokens/hour.

batch_discount.value: 50% off standard price (Batch/Flex: input $0.15/1M, output $1.25/1M, cached $0.02/1M). Priority tier: input $0.54/1M, output $4.50/1M, cached $0.05/1M.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: All modalities bill at the standard input rate -- no separate audio line on this card. Conversions: image 258 tokens per <=384px image or per 768x768 tile; audio 32 tokens/sec; video 263 tokens/sec. Grounding with Google Search or Maps billed separately: 5,000 free requests per month, then $14 per 1,000.

input_output_shared.notes: CHANGED from true. Google publishes 'Input token limit: 1,048,576' and 'Output token limit: 65,536' as two separate limits and never documents a single shared pool. Medium confidence -- the relationship is not stated explicitly either way.

audio_token_rule.notes: Video converts at 263 tokens per second.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Docs: 'a token is equivalent to about 4 characters'.

native_mcp.notes: RE-SOURCED 2026-08-19 to Google's published google-genai SDK documentation, which states 'Built-in MCP support is an experimental feature' and shows a local MCP ClientSession passed straight into tools=[session] with automatic function calling (example model: gemini-2.5-flash). That CLIENT-SIDE path is what makes native_mcp true for this model. The previously cited Interactions API overview does NOT support the claim for this model -- its limitations section says 'Gemini 3 does not support remote MCP, this is coming soon' (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions-overview). The server-side 'mcp_server' tool type documented on https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling is exercised there only with gemini-3.7-flash, and remote MCP is Streamable-HTTP only ('SSE (Server-Sent Events) servers are not supported'). MCP tools only -- resources and prompts are not consumed. Confidence medium: the supported path is an SDK feature the vendor labels experimental, and the two vendor pages conflict on remote MCP.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Verbatim: 'The model supports calling multiple functions in a single turn (parallel function calling)' and 'in sequence (compositional function calling)'.

max_tools_hard.notes: TIER 4 / OBSERVED API ERROR, NOT PUBLISHED SPEC (re-graded 2026-08-19 from tier 2 -- a GitHub issue is tier 4 under methodology section 4 even when it quotes a real API rejection). The cited Gemini CLI issue (opened 2026-02-14, closed 'not planned') reports the verbatim API rejection 'At most 512 function declarations can be specified' when many MCP servers are enabled. UNCONFIRMED BY VENDOR DOCS: on 2026-08-19 I opened the Gemini API function-calling docs (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling -- no numeric cap, only the best practice 'Keep active set to 10-20 tools maximum'), the Interactions API overview (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions-overview), the Live API tools page (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/tools), the Vertex REST FunctionDeclaration reference and the Gemini Enterprise / Vertex function-calling reference; none of them publishes a maximum number of function declarations. The only tier-1 count Google publishes sits on a DIFFERENT surface: Firebase AI Logic states 'The maximum number of function declarations that you can provide with the request is 128' (https://firebase.google.com/docs/ai-logic/function-calling), presented there as a Firebase AI Logic SDK constraint. Planning guidance: 128 is the conservative documented number on that SDK; 512 is the observed hard rejection point on the raw API. SCOPE: aggregate -- summed across every connected MCP server plus built-in tools in one request; there is no per-MCP-server cap.

max_tools_practical.notes: Google's own function-calling best practices state: 'Tool Selection: Keep active set to 10-20 tools maximum.' Recorded at the top of that band (20). This is vendor ADVICE, not an enforced cap and not a measured cliff, hence medium confidence. Searched for Gemini-specific empirical tool-count degradation data and found none: the most recent public study (Superhuman, June 2026, 584-tool / 110-agent catalog, flat-routing F1 58.2% at 51 tools falling to 42.1% at 584) tested GPT-5.4, GPT-5.1 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 only -- no Google models. The limits that DO bind for Gemini: this ~10-20 advisory band, the 512 aggregate declaration ceiling (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard), and the 1,048,576-token input window.

tool_definition_shape.notes: functionDeclarations[] inside a Tool object: {name, description, parameters (OpenAPI/JSON-Schema subset)}. The Interactions API additionally accepts a tool of type 'mcp_server' {name, url, headers, allowed_tools} that is expanded server-side rather than serialized by the caller.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool/function declarations are serialized into the request and billed as input tokens. Since the 2026 token-accounting update the usage payload breaks them out as total_tool_use_tokens, so the definition footprint can be measured directly instead of inferred.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No deferred/lazy tool loading at the model-API layer -- there is no Gemini analogue of Anthropic's tool-search / defer_loading. Two partial mitigations exist and are NOT the same thing: (a) the Interactions API mcp_server tool takes an allowed_tools allowlist, a static pre-filter applied before definitions reach the model; (b) implicit/explicit context caching amortizes a static tool block. Gemini CLI's Agent Skills do use progressive disclosure, but that defers SKILL.md bodies, not tool definitions.

max_tool_name_len.notes: RE-SOURCED 2026-08-19 to Google's own FunctionDeclaration reference (the previous citation was an unrelated third-party repo issue, tier 4). Firebase's FunctionDeclaration reference states verbatim: 'The name of the function to call. Must start with a letter or an underscore. Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a max length of 64.' Google's Vertex AI REST FunctionDeclaration reference carries the same constraint with dots also allowed: 'Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores, dots and dashes, with a maximum length of 64.' SCOPE: per-tool, API-enforced. This bites MCP servers because hosts namespace tool names -- Gemini CLI prefixes every MCP tool as mcp_{serverName}_{toolName} and truncates names over 63 characters, so a long server name silently eats the 64-character budget.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented character or token cap on function/tool description strings; re-checked 2026-08-19 against the function-calling page and the Interactions API reference, which document description as an untyped optional string. The effective constraints are the 1,048,576-token input window and the undocumented 'very large or deeply nested schemas' rejection.

max_request_size.notes: Verbatim: inline data '100 MB per request or payload' with '50 MB for PDFs'; external/signed URLs '100 MB per request/payload'. Larger payloads go through the Files API ('2 GB per file, up to 20GB per project', retained '48 Hours'). This is the HTTP payload ceiling; for text + tool-definition traffic the 1,048,576-token input limit binds first.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-functionResponse size cap in bytes or tokens. Gemini 3 models accept multimodal function responses (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain inline in the response part) and require each response to carry a matching call_id and name. Tool results consume the same 1,048,576-token input budget as everything else.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel function calling is supported with no documented numeric cap on how many calls may be emitted in one turn. Gemini 3 returns a unique id per function call and requires exactly one response per call, matched by id and name -- results may return out of order but must be 1:1.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.unit: automatic function-calling remote calls per request (SDK default)
tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: CHANGED from null. SCOPE: SDK layer, not the model API. The google-genai SDK's automatic function calling loops with a default maximum of 10 remote calls per request; it is configurable and can be disabled, after which the caller drives the loop. The Gemini API itself documents no per-turn numeric cap on tool-call/result cycles -- there is no 'reached its tool-use limit' error analogous to Claude's, so the limits that actually bind a long agentic run are the 512-declaration aggregate ceiling (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard) and the 1,048,576-token input window. The Interactions API does not support Python automatic function calling at all. Source re-pointed 2026-08-19 from the googleapis/python-genai GitHub repo to Google's published SDK documentation site, which states verbatim: 'by default the SDK will perform automatic function calling until the remote calls exceed the maximum remote call for automatic function calling (default to 10 times)'.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented cap on simultaneous MCP server connections at the API layer, and the Interactions API reference documents no numeric cap on how many mcp_server tools an interaction may carry. The binding constraint is the 512 aggregate functionDeclarations (an observed API rejection, tier 4 -- see max_tools_hard). Client layer for contrast: Gemini CLI users report tools being 'silently dropped' past roughly 100 aggregate MCP tools (https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21823, closed), and Gemini CLI's docs set a 600,000 ms (10 minute) default per-server request timeout.

The only tier-1 count Google publishes sits on a DIFFERENT surface: Firebase AI Logic states 'The maximum number of function declarations that you can provide with the request is 128' (https://firebase.google.com/docs/ai-logic/function-calling), presented there as a Firebase AI Logic SDK constraint. Planning guidance: 128 is the conservative documented number on that SDK; 512 is the observed hard rejection point on the raw API. SCOPE: aggregate client/API ceiling, identical in substance to max_tools_hard -- summed across every connected MCP server plus built-in tools in one request; there is no per-MCP-server cap.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Only a subset of the OpenAPI schema is accepted for function parameters (verbatim: 'Only a subset of the OpenAPI schema is supported'). Gemini 3-series and 2.5-series models accept type, nullable, required, format, description, properties, items, enum, anyOf, $ref, minItems, maxItems, minimum, maximum. Documented soft constraint, verbatim: 'For any mode, the API may reject very large or deeply nested schemas' -- Google publishes no numeric nesting-depth or property-count cap, so there is nothing analogous to OpenAI strict mode's 100-property / 5-level rules. Function names are validated by the API against 'Must start with a letter or an underscore. Must be alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), underscores (_), dots (.), colons (:), or dashes (-), with a maximum length of 64.' For MCP the function-calling page adds: 'MCP server names should not include the - character. Use snake_case server names instead.' Sources: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling , https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode/issues/235
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: RATE LIMITS: Google no longer publishes per-model RPM/TPM/RPD tables -- the rate-limits page now says limits 'can be viewed in Google AI Studio' (only Batch API enqueued-token quotas remain tabulated), so the per-model rate numbers carried in the 2026-06-21 revision of this dataset are no longer sourceable and have been removed rather than restated. API CHANGES since 2026-06-21: the Interactions API went GA in June 2026 and is now the recommended surface for all new projects; the sampling parameters temperature / top_p / top_k were deprecated 2026-07-21; thinking_budget is replaced by thinking_level. The Interactions API does NOT support explicit context caching (implicit only, via previous_interaction_id), the Batch API, or Python automatic function calling. Tool configuration is interaction-scoped and must be re-sent on every interaction, so tool-definition tokens are re-paid per interaction unless implicit caching hits. Token accounting now exposes total_tool_use_tokens, total_thought_tokens and total_cached_tokens in the usage payload -- total_tool_use_tokens makes an MCP server's definition footprint directly measurable. MODEL-SPECIFIC: DEPRECATED with shutdown 2027-05-07 -- do not plan new MCP deployments on this model; the documented replacement is gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Audio input is billed at 2x the text rate on this card ($0.50 vs $0.25/1M), which the replacement no longer does. Computer Use is not supported.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode. Gemini enforces its own looser OpenAPI-subset keyword rules plus an undocumented size/nesting rejection -- captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.

skills_supported.notes: CHANGED from false. Google now ships Agent Skills: a SKILL.md-based, model-invokable instruction bundle with an official library (github.com/google-gemini/gemini-skills, Apache-2.0), publicised 2026-03-25 and documented on ai.google.dev. IMPORTANT SCOPE: skills live at the AGENT/CLI layer (Gemini CLI, Antigravity, third-party coding assistants), not in the model API -- the Gemini docs state 'Most agents index skills only on startup' and the generateContent / Interactions endpoints neither accept nor process a skill object. For a raw API caller the only always-on instruction channel is still system_instruction, and Gems remain a consumer-product feature.

skills_loading_model.notes: Verbatim (Gemini CLI): 'At the start of a session, Gemini CLI scans the discovery tiers and injects the name and description of all enabled skills into the system prompt' and 'Only skill metadata (name and description) is loaded initially. Detailed instructions and resources are only disclosed when the model explicitly activates the skill, saving context tokens.' Activation is itself a tool call (activate_skill), after which 'The SKILL.md body and folder structure is added to the conversation history'.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Skills never enter a Gemini API request as a first-class object -- the agent host injects skill name+description into the system prompt at session start and appends the SKILL.md body only after activate_skill fires. The resident cost is therefore one metadata line per enabled skill and the burst cost is the skill body, both billed as ordinary input tokens. System instructions are billed as input on every request; caching can absorb a static instruction + tool-definition prefix once it clears the model's minimum cacheable size.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System instructions are counted as part of the input tokens; Google documents no fixed per-request overhead beyond the caller-supplied content. In the Interactions API tools and system instructions are interaction-scoped and must be re-specified on every interaction, so a large MCP tool block is re-billed each turn unless implicit caching hits.

Cached read $0.025/1M (text/image/video), $0.05/1M (audio); cache storage $1.00/1M tokens/hour. The caching page's minimum-cacheable-prompt table lists no Flash-Lite row, so that threshold is undocumented for this model. Explicit caches are not supported in the Interactions API.
