The tool-search guide adds 'aim to keep each namespace to fewer than 10 functions for better token efficiency and model performance' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search). Consistent with the long-standing tier-4 community/Berkeley-FCL observation that tool-selection accuracy starts degrading somewhere in the 30-50 tool range. Confidence medium: it is vendor advice about behaviour, not an enforced limit.

tool_definition_shape.notes: OpenAI function/tool JSON: {type:'function', name, description, parameters, strict}. The guide states functions 'are injected into the system message in a syntax the model has been trained on', so shape directly determines the token count.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Token-counting guide, verbatim: 'Tool definitions (function schemas, MCP servers, etc.) add tokens to the context. Count them together with your input.' The function-calling guide adds that function definitions 'count against the model's context limit and are billed as input tokens.'

tool_search_deferral.notes: Model page lists 'Tool search: Supported'. gpt-5.4 is the earliest model with tool_search — 'tool search is supported on gpt-5.4 and later models'. Pair with the MCP tool's defer_loading to keep a large server catalog out of the up-front tools array.

max_tool_name_len.notes: CHANGED from 64 (2026-06-21). The Responses API reference now documents the function tool's `name` as minLength 1 / maxLength 128. The previously cited 64-character cap could no longer be found on any currently-reachable OpenAI page — the function-calling guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling) no longer states a name length or pattern at all. Confidence medium because the older 64-char Chat-Completions figure is still widely repeated downstream and the two surfaces may differ. Practical impact is unchanged: MCP clients namespace tool names ('<server>_<tool>'), and that prefix is spent from this budget.

max_tool_description_len.notes: Confidence downgraded medium -> low on 2026-08-19. Still undocumented on any OpenAI page: the Responses and Chat references say the description 'has a maximum length' without printing the number. The only public evidence remains the API error text "Invalid 'tools[1].function.description': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 1024" reported in the linked thread (2024-09-22, last activity 2025-03-27). Not re-confirmed against GPT-5.6 in this pass. Mitigation is unchanged: move long guidance out of the tool description and into the system prompt or a skill.

max_request_size.notes: NUMERIC + NARROW SCOPE (fixed 2026-08-19; was the malformed string '512MB' with unit 'bytes'). The only per-request byte ceiling OpenAI publishes is on the images/vision guide, verbatim 'Up to 512 MB total payload size per request' alongside 'Up to 1500 individual image inputs per request' -- i.e. it is documented for requests carrying image inputs, not as a general JSON body limit. No general request-body byte cap is documented for Chat Completions or the Responses API (checked the API references and the rate-limits guide on 2026-08-19). Do NOT read this as directly comparable to Anthropic's 32 MB or Gemini's 100 MB general request ceilings. For MCP work the binding ceiling is the token side: tool definitions and tool results are input tokens against the context window, not bytes.

max_tool_result_size.notes: EMPIRICAL, not spec (tier 4, low confidence). Value made numeric 2026-08-19 (was the string '512KB'). Re-opened the cited OpenAI developer-forum thread: it reports a 512KB ceiling on submitted tool output, and its own respondent states "I can't find anywhere within the documentation that states this limit exists" -- still undocumented on any OpenAI page, and not re-confirmed against the GPT-5.6 Responses API. Independently, tool RESULTS are ordinary input tokens on the next turn, so a chatty tool consumes the context window regardless of any byte cap; Programmatic Tool Calling is OpenAI's documented mitigation because the program can filter intermediate results before they reach the model.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: No per-request numeric cap on how many tool calls the model may emit in one turn is documented; parallel_tool_calls is a boolean, and the only documented setting is false, which forces exactly zero or one call. What does bind: the size of the aggregate tools array (no vendor-published numeric cap -- see max_tools_hard), the context window that every call and result is charged against, and the per-tier MCP tool-call rate limits (200/1000/2000 RPM).

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No API-enforced cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn is documented; the agents guide describes the loop as SDK-provided and application-managed ('SDK sessions', 'Conversations API', manual history, resumable run state) and prints no numeric ceiling. What bounds a run in practice: the context window, the cost/rate limits, and whatever max-turns guard the calling SDK sets.

max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric cap on connected MCP servers is documented for either the Responses API or ChatGPT. The ChatGPT help article confirms a workspace 'can invoke multiple first-party and third-party apps in a single prompt' without printing a ceiling. The limits that actually bind are aggregate: the size of the tools array summed over all servers (no vendor-published numeric cap -- see max_tools_hard), and the context window those definitions are charged to.

max_total_tools.notes: AGGREGATE ceiling across every connected MCP server plus built-in tools, in one request. Null for the same reason as max_tools_hard: no current OpenAI page publishes a numeric ceiling on the tools array. Verified 2026-08-19 against the function-calling guide (this source_url), the Responses API reference (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/api-reference/responses/create -- no maxItems on tools), the Chat Completions reference and the tool-search guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search). The previously recorded 128 came from the Assistants API deep-dive, a per-Assistant cap on an API that shuts down 2026-08-26, and has been withdrawn. Budget allocation is therefore governed by the context window (tool definitions are input tokens), OpenAI's 'fewer than 20 functions at the start of a turn' guidance, and the per-namespace 'fewer than 10 functions' advice for deferred tools; no vendor page publishes a ceiling on how many tools may be registered behind tool search.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Function/tool `parameters` use OpenAI's Structured Outputs JSON Schema subset. Strict mode (strict:true) requires additionalProperties:false on every object and every property listed in 'required'; the root object may not be anyOf; anyOf members must themselves stay in the subset. Unsupported (silently dropped / rejected) keywords per Microsoft Foundry's Azure OpenAI mirror of this page (last updated 2026-08-06, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/structured-outputs): string minLength/maxLength/pattern/format; number minimum/maximum/multipleOf; object patternProperties/unevaluatedProperties/propertyNames/minProperties/maxProperties; array unevaluatedItems/contains/minContains/maxContains/minItems/maxItems/uniqueItems. SIZE-LIMIT CONFLICT (recorded, unresolved): the Azure mirror still states '100 object properties total' and '5 levels of nesting', while OpenAI announced raised limits on 2025-07-11 (5,000 properties, 120,000 characters per string, 1,000 enum values, 15,000 total chars across enum members when >250 values) as relayed at https://community.openai.com/t/structured-outputs-limits-are-raised-to-support-larger-schemas/1313593 (tier 3, community relay of an @OpenAIDevs post). OpenAI's own current Structured Outputs page (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs) links to a 'supported schemas' detail page that no longer resolves, so no tier-1 OpenAI page currently states either set of numbers. Treat 100 properties / 5 levels as the conservative floor and 5,000 / 10 as unconfirmed. No documented byte-size cap on the serialized tool-definition payload beyond the context window itself.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Remote MCP (Responses API, https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp): a server is attached with server_url / connector_id / tunnel_id; its tool definitions are fetched at request time and billed as input tokens ('we charge for tokens used when importing tool definitions or making tool calls. There are no additional fees involved per tool call'). No per-server or per-request cap on the NUMBER of MCP servers is documented — the binding ceiling is the aggregate size of the tools array (no vendor-published numeric cap -- see max_tools_hard) plus the context window. allowed_tools filters which of a server's tools are exposed; defer_loading hands discovery to tool search; allowed_callers ['direct','programmatic'] gates whether a tool is reachable from Programmatic Tool Calling; require_approval ('always' default / 'never' / per-tool_names filter) gates writes. MCP tool-call rate limits: 200 RPM (tier 1), 1000 RPM (tiers 2-3), 2000 RPM (tiers 4-5). Programmatic Tool Calling (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling) lets the model emit JavaScript that runs in an isolated V8 runtime and orchestrates tools, which 'can reduce the amount of intermediate tool output added to model context'; no numeric limits on tools, result size or runtime are published, and a running program cannot itself invoke tool search. ChatGPT-product MCP (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-apps-and-full-mcp-connectors-in-chatgpt-beta): full MCP with write actions is in beta for Business/Enterprise/Edu; Pro is read/fetch only; multiple first- and third-party apps may be invoked in one prompt with no published app-count cap. Per-model RPM/TPM rate limits apply and are listed on each model page. Programmatic Tool Calling is listed as supported on this model's page.

strict_function_schema.notes: Structured Outputs strict mode applies to function/tool parameters: additionalProperties:false everywhere, all properties required, root may not be anyOf, and a documented list of unsupported keywords. See tool_schema_limits_notes for the unresolved 100-vs-5,000 property-count conflict.

skills_supported.notes: Model page lists 'Skills: Supported'.

skills_loading_model.notes: Progressive disclosure, not always-on injection: a skill is 'a versioned bundle of files plus a SKILL.md manifest', and the platform adds only each skill's name, description and path to prompt context; the model reads the full SKILL.md only when it decides to invoke the skill.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Two-stage cost. Stage 1 (always paid, per request): the name + description + path stub for every attached skill. Stage 2 (paid only on invocation): the full SKILL.md body, and any bundled files the model reads. Docs are explicit that 'Skill instructions are user prompt input (not system prompt input), so they're handled with the same priority as other user-provided instructions' — which also means they are ordinary input tokens. Ingest caps documented 2026-08-19: 50 MB max zip upload, 500 max files per skill version, 25 MB max uncompressed file. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-skills.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: The Responses API prepends hidden scaffolding for every enabled surface (MCP server tool lists, skill stubs, hosted-tool definitions). OpenAI does not publish its token size. Measure it empirically by POSTing the same payload with and without each tool to /v1/responses/input_tokens (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/token-counting) and differencing.

prompt_caching.notes: Automatic caching from the 1,024-token minimum. gpt-5.4 is listed under Extended Prompt Cache Retention (up to 24h) in addition to the short in-memory tier; cached input bills at 0.1x, and there is no 1.25x cache-write surcharge (that starts with GPT-5.6). Tool definitions, tool ordering and structured-output schemas are part of the cached prefix.

memory_feature.notes: No model-side persistent memory in the API. The agents guide frames state as application-managed — SDK sessions, the Conversations API, manual history, or resumable run state. ChatGPT's 'Memory' and Codex's memories are product features, not this model's API surface.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Unchanged. Standard processing under 272K input tokens; regional data-residency processing adds a 10% uplift.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Unchanged.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Unchanged; 0.1x the uncached input rate.

batch_discount.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image input billed as input tokens via 32x32 patch counting (auto == high on this model, i.e. a 2,500-patch ceiling by default). Audio not supported.

release_date.notes: From the dated snapshot gpt-5.4-2026-03-05, still listed. Re-verified 2026-08-19.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Unchanged: August 31, 2025.

detail.notes: SUPERSEDED but still GA. Was the API default flagship at the 2026-06-21 snapshot; as of 2026-08-19 it sits in the 'More models' section of https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/all with GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna above it on https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models, and carries no deprecation entry on https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations. Snapshot gpt-5.4-2026-03-05. Now also lists Programmatic Tool Calling as supported. Status left at 'ga' — no vendor page deprecates it, and the schema status enum has no 'superseded' value.

context_window_tokens.notes: Unchanged at 400,000 — the smallest window in this roster and the one most likely to be bound by a large MCP tool surface.

input_output_shared.notes: Single shared pool.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived: 400,000 - 128,000 = 272,000. Not published separately.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Not separately published.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Unchanged — 128,000, i.e. nearly a third of this model's whole window.

extended_context.notes: 400,000 is the GA window; no extended mode documented.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: reasoning_effort: none (default), low, medium, high, xhigh. Reasoning tokens bill as output.

tokenizer_family.notes: tiktoken's model.py maps the GPT-5 family to o200k_base via MODEL_TO_ENCODING ('gpt-5') and the 'gpt-5-' prefix entry in MODEL_PREFIX_TO_ENCODING; no encoding newer than o200k_base exists for the hosted GPT-5.x models (o200k_harmony is the open-weight gpt-oss variant). Source changed from a tiktoken issue thread to the mapping file itself.

tokenizer_public.notes: tiktoken is open source (MIT) on GitHub and PyPI, so GPT-5.x token counts are reproducible offline — unusual among frontier vendors.

tokenizer_access.notes: pip install tiktoken; encodings o200k_base and cl100k_base ship with the package.

count_tokens_method.value: Server-side (exact, includes tools): POST /v1/responses/input_tokens with the same payload you would send to responses.create. Offline estimate: import tiktoken; enc = tiktoken.get_encoding('o200k_base'); len(enc.encode(text)).
count_tokens_method.notes: CHANGED: the token-counting guide now documents a dedicated endpoint, POST /v1/responses/input_tokens, which accepts text, messages, images, files, tools and conversations and returns an exact count — the correct way to measure an MCP server's startup footprint, since local tiktoken cannot reproduce the hidden tool/skill scaffolding or image patching. Previous entry cited include=['usage'] round-trips instead.

image_token_rule.value: Patch-based (32x32 pixel patches), same GPT-5.x scheme as gpt-5.4: detail low / high / original / auto, up to 2,500 patches at high and 10,000 at original, token cost = patch count x a model-specific multiplier. Image input only.
image_token_rule.notes: CHANGED from the legacy 85+170-per-tile rule. Confidence is low because the vision guide enumerates gpt-5.6 / gpt-5.5 / gpt-5.4 explicitly but does not print a separate row or multiplier for gpt-5.4-mini; the family scheme is assumed. Measure with POST /v1/responses/input_tokens.

audio_token_rule.notes: Model page lists Audio: not supported (text and image input, text output only). Audio work goes to the gpt-realtime / gpt-transcribe families, which are separate models and out of scope for this entry.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Source corrected on 2026-08-19: the previously cited tiktoken cookbook does not in fact state a ratio. OpenAI's help article does: '1 token ~ 4 characters' and '1 token ~ 3/4 of a word' for English. Rule of thumb only — JSON tool definitions tokenize denser than prose, so use the input_tokens endpoint for footprint numbers.

function_calling.notes: Model page lists 'Function calling: Supported'.

native_mcp.notes: Model page lists 'MCP: Supported'. Remote MCP servers attach as a first-class tool type on the Responses API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).

parallel_tool_calls.notes: The function-calling guide documents parallel_tool_calls and states that setting it to false 'ensures exactly zero or one tool is called'; default behaviour allows multiple tool calls in one turn.

max_tools_hard.notes: AGGREGATE scope (all connected MCP servers + built-in/hosted tools in one request's tools array). NO CURRENT TIER-1 PAGE STATES A NUMERIC CAP, so the value is null. Pages opened 2026-08-19: the function-calling guide (this source_url) states no maximum and instead says 'Aim for fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn at any one time, though this is just a soft suggestion'; the Responses API reference (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/api-reference/responses/create) documents no maxItems on the tools array; the Chat Completions reference (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/api-reference/chat/create) documents no count limit; the tool-search guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search) gives only a 'fewer than 10 functions' per-namespace best practice. It will shut down on August 26, 2026' -- so it is not evidence for the GPT-5.x Responses/Chat Completions tools array. skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: The Responses API prepends hidden scaffolding for every enabled surface (MCP server tool lists, skill stubs, hosted-tool definitions). Measure it empirically by POSTing the same payload with and without each tool to /v1/responses/input_tokens (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/token-counting) and differencing.

prompt_caching.notes: Automatic caching from the 1,024-token minimum; cached input bills at 0.1x ($0.075/1M). Confidence caveat: the prompt-caching guide's Extended Prompt Cache Retention list names gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.2, gpt-5.1 variants, gpt-5 and gpt-4.1 but does NOT name gpt-5.4-mini, so 24h retention on this model is not confirmed — the standard short in-memory tier should be assumed. Previous entry asserted 24h; corrected 2026-08-19.

memory_feature.notes: No model-side persistent memory in the API. The agents guide frames state as application-managed — SDK sessions, the Conversations API, manual history, or resumable run state. ChatGPT's 'Memory' and Codex's memories are product features, not this model's API surface.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Unchanged.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Unchanged; 0.1x the uncached input rate.

batch_discount.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image input billed as input tokens via the GPT-5.x 32x32 patch scheme. Audio not supported.

release_date.notes: From the dated snapshot gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17, still listed. Re-verified 2026-08-19.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Unchanged: August 31, 2025.

detail.notes: SUPERSEDED but still GA. Still listed under 'More models' on https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/all with no deprecation entry on https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations; GPT-5.6 Luna is the closest current-generation replacement (and is both cheaper and 1.05M-context). Status left at 'ga' — no vendor deprecation, and the schema status enum has no 'superseded' value.

context_window_tokens.notes: Model card: 'Context window: 500,000'. Pricing table also lists grok-4.6 at 500k. NOTE this is HALF of grok-4.3's 1M window — the flagship moved down in context while moving up in price, so an MCP tool surface occupies twice the share of the window it did on grok-4.3.

input_output_shared.notes: xAI does not state separate input/output pools; the OpenAI-compatible convention (one shared window) is implied and the model card publishes a single 'Context window' number. Medium confidence — not explicitly documented.

max_input_tokens.notes: No max-input cap is documented separately from the 500k window. Not derived, because no max-output figure is published to subtract.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: No default max-output value is published on the model card or in the API reference (checked 2026-08-19). max_tokens is accepted through the OpenAI-compatible surface but its default is not documented.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: No maximum single-completion cap is published. What binds is the 500k shared window; xAI documents no separate per-response numeric ceiling.

extended_context.notes: No beta/extended window beyond 500k. The 200k figure that appears in pricing is a LONG-CONTEXT PRICING threshold, not a window: 'Models with long context pricing bill the long context rates for all tokens in a request once its prompt reaches the model's long context threshold' (grok-4.6: >= 200k).

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: 'Reasoning tokens: Full completion token price' — reasoning tokens bill at the output rate and are reported via reasoning_tokens in usage. The reasoning docs add: 'reasoning_effort defaults to high. Reasoning cannot be disabled.'

No Grok-specific measurement exists. xAI's own mitigation guidance is allowed_tools: 'Reduce context overhead by limiting tool definitions the model needs to consider.' On grok-4.6 the 500k window (half of grok-4.3's) makes definition bloat bite sooner in context terms.

tool_definition_shape.notes: OpenAI-compatible {type:'function', name, description, parameters} tool objects; the OpenAI SDK works against the xAI base_url. Remote MCP tools are declared as {type:'mcp', server_url, server_label, ...}.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool definitions are serialized into the request and billed as input tokens. Pricing page confirms MCP tools are 'Token-based only' — no per-invocation fee, but every definition token is charged at the input rate.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No progressive tool disclosure / tool-search mechanism is documented. allowed_tools is a static per-request allow-list chosen by the caller, not runtime deferral; there is no xAI equivalent of Claude's tool-search / defer_loading. Re-checked the tools overview and remote-MCP pages on 2026-08-19.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No character limit on tool/function names is documented — the schema reference lists name as a required string ('Unique identifier (max 200 tools per request)') with no length constraint, and publishes no equivalent to OpenAI's 64-character cap. Remote MCP tool names additionally carry a '<server_label>.' prefix for tool-call prefixing, with no documented cap on the combined length.

max_tool_description_len.notes: Tool description length carries no documented numeric limit; description is required ('What the tool does — helps the model decide when to use it') with no character or token limit stated. What binds in practice is the 500k context window.

max_request_size.notes: No maximum request payload size (bytes/MB) is published anywhere in the docs — checked the API reference, function-calling, remote-MCP, tools-overview and rate-limit pages on 2026-08-19. The only published payload ceiling is per-image ('Maximum image size: 20MiB'). What binds a request is the 500k context window and the tokens-per-minute rate limit.

max_tool_result_size.notes: Tool result/output size carries no documented numeric limit. Server-side tool output is consumed inside xAI's agentic loop; client-side function results are appended to the conversation as strings with no stated size limit, so what binds is the 500k context window.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: No numeric cap on how many tool calls the model may emit in one response is documented. Parallel calling is on by default and can be switched off with parallel_tool_calls: false; max_turns limits assistant turns, and explicitly 'does not directly limit the number of individual tool calls'.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: max_turns bounds the agentic loop, not tool calls: 'max_turns does not directly limit the number of individual tool calls. max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric cap on simultaneous Remote MCP server connections per request is documented; the multi-server example wires three servers (distinct server_url/server_label) in one request with no stated ceiling. The limits that actually bind are AGGREGATE: the 200-tool per-request cap covering every connected server's tools plus any custom functions and built-in tools, and the 500k context window.

max_total_tools.notes: The 200-tool per-request cap IS the aggregate ceiling for grok-4.6: xAI documents no separate "tools across all servers" limit, so custom function tools + built-in server-side tools + every tool exposed by every connected MCP server are counted against the same 200. Scope: aggregate per request, not per MCP server. Asserted only for grok-4.6 because that is the only model the citing page names. tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Function-calling schema reference (re-read 2026-08-19): name = 'Unique identifier (max 200 tools per request)'; description = 'What the tool does — helps the model decide when to use it'; parameters = 'JSON Schema defining function inputs'. Root-schema rule was WIDENED since the 2026-06-21 snapshot: the parameters root must be an object, but 'A root anyOf or oneOf also works when every branch is itself an object'; a root that is a scalar, an array, or an anyOf/oneOf with a non-object branch is 'rejected with a 400 error'. No documented depth, property-count or enum-size limits. Remote MCP tools are prefixed by server_label ('A label to identify the server (used for tool call prefixing)'). Without allowed_tools, 'all tool definitions exposed by the MCP server are automatically injected into the model's context'. grok-4.6 supports reasoning effort low/medium/high(default)/xhigh; xhigh is grok-4.6-and-later only.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Remote MCP: Streaming HTTP and SSE transports only (no stdio); require_approval and connector_id from the OpenAI Responses API are not supported. Server-side built-in tool invocation fees (pricing page, 2026-08-19): web_search $5/1k calls, x_search $5/1k calls, code_execution $5/1k calls, attachment_search $10/1k calls, collections_search $2.50/1k calls; Remote MCP tools are 'Token-based only'. Only successfully executed server-side tools are billed (server_side_tool_usage), not every attempted call. Priority processing (service_tier: 'priority') bills all token types at 2x standard rates. Context Compaction is OPT-IN (corrected 2026-08-19): it is an explicit call to POST /v1/responses/compact or chat.compact(), not automatic. max_turns caps assistant/server-side turns in the agentic loop and 'If max_turns is not specified, the server applies a global default cap' whose value xAI does not publish. Rate limits (2026-08-19): 150 requests/second and 50M tokens/minute at Tier 0, rising to 500 RPS / 100M TPM at Tier 4 — roughly 4x grok-4.3's throughput. Regions us-east-1 and us-west-2. grok-4.6 is NOT batch-discount eligible. Long-context pricing starts at a 200k prompt and re-rates the entire request.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode is documented. The only schema constraint xAI publishes is the parameters-root rule (object, or anyOf/oneOf whose branches are all objects); no 100-property / 5-depth / no-oneOf enforcement mode exists.

skills_supported.notes: No API-level skills primitive. skills_loading_model.notes: Not applicable at the API layer. The only Grok-side progressive disclosure is in the Grok Build CLI, where user-invocable skills appear as slash commands rather than being preloaded.

skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: No fixed system-prompt overhead is documented; system-prompt tokens bill as input at $2.00/1M short-context ($0.50/1M if served from cache, $4.00/$1.00 under long-context pricing).

prompt_caching.notes: Prompt caching applies: cached prompt tokens are 'billed at the cached prompt token price, which is substantially lower than the regular prompt token price', and the pricing table lists a $0.50/1M cached-input rate for grok-4.6 ($1.00/1M long-context). Cache hits are reported via cached_tokens. NOTE grok-4.6's cache discount is shallower than grok-4.3's ($0.50 vs $0.20/1M, i.e. 25% of input vs 16%).

memory_feature.notes: No persistent cross-session memory is exposed by the API. input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Short-context rate (prompt below the model's long-context threshold, 200k tokens). At/above the threshold LONG-context rates bill ALL tokens in the request: $4.00/1M input. grok-4.6 is 60% more expensive on input and 140% more expensive on output than grok-4.3.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Short-context output rate; long-context output rate is $12.00/1M once the prompt reaches the 200k long-context threshold.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cached-input rate; $1.00/1M under long-context pricing. Cached tokens still count toward the long-context threshold: 'Long context pricing applies when total prompt tokens (including cached tokens) exceed the model's long context threshold.'

batch_discount.notes: Pricing page batch section lists only 'grok-4.3, grok-4.20-0309-reasoning, grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning, grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309' at 20% off and states 'Models not listed above have no batch discount.' grok-4.6 is therefore not batch-discounted. Priority processing instead bills 2x standard on all token types.

billing_unit.notes: Billed per token for model usage; built-in server-side tools add a separate per-invocation fee, while Remote MCP tools are 'Token-based only'.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image input bills as input tokens; xAI publishes no tile/patch formula, so per-image cost must be measured empirically. Per-image ceiling is 20MiB, jpg/jpeg or png. No audio on this model.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Prompt-caching usage-and-pricing page (re-read 2026-08-19) lists the billed token types: 'Prompt tokens (non-cached): Full prompt token price', 'Cached prompt tokens: Reduced cached prompt token price', 'Completion tokens: Full completion token price', 'Reasoning tokens: Full completion token price'. Reasoning usage is exposed as reasoning_tokens.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode is documented. The only schema constraint xAI publishes is the parameters-root rule (object, or anyOf/oneOf whose branches are all objects); no 100-property / 5-depth / no-oneOf enforcement mode exists.

skills_supported.notes: No API-level skills primitive. Grok Build skills ('reusable folders containing markdown instructions, script files, and resources for agents', surfaced as /<skill-name> slash commands) are a CLI/product feature, not an API mechanism that injects packaged context into a model request.

skills_loading_model.notes: Not applicable at the API layer. The only Grok-side progressive disclosure is in the Grok Build CLI, where user-invocable skills appear as slash commands rather than being preloaded.

skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: No fixed system-prompt overhead documented; system-prompt tokens bill as input at $2.00/1M ($0.30/1M cached, $4.00/$0.60 under long-context pricing).

prompt_caching.notes: Pricing table lists a cached-input rate of $0.30/1M for grok-4.5 ($0.60/1M long-context), and the caching docs state cached tokens are 'billed at the cached prompt token price, which is substantially lower than the regular prompt token price'. grok-4.5's cache rate is cheaper than grok-4.6's ($0.30 vs $0.50/1M).

memory_feature.notes: No persistent memory in the API. Context Compaction (opt-in, POST /v1/responses/compact) and store_messages/previous_response_id or use_encrypted_content are the documented state-carrying mechanisms.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Short-context rate (prompt below the model's long-context threshold, 200k tokens). At/above the threshold LONG-context rates bill ALL tokens in the request: $4.00/1M input. Same headline rates as grok-4.6 but a cheaper cache tier ($0.30 vs $0.50/1M).

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Short-context output rate; long-context output rate is $12.00/1M once the prompt reaches the 200k long-context threshold.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cached-input rate; $0.60/1M under long-context pricing. Cached tokens still count toward the long-context threshold: 'Long context pricing applies when total prompt tokens (including cached tokens) exceed the model's long context threshold.'

batch_discount.notes: Pricing page lists batch eligibility for grok-4.3 and the grok-4.20 variants only, at 20% off, and states 'Models not listed above have no batch discount.' grok-4.5 is not on that list.

billing_unit.notes: Billed per token for model usage; built-in server-side tools add a separate per-invocation fee, while Remote MCP tools are 'Token-based only'.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image input bills as input tokens with no published tile/patch formula; 20MiB per image, jpg/jpeg or png. No audio.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Prompt-caching usage-and-pricing page (re-read 2026-08-19) lists the billed token types: 'Prompt tokens (non-cached): Full prompt token price', 'Cached prompt tokens: Reduced cached prompt token price', 'Completion tokens: Full completion token price', 'Reasoning tokens: Full completion token price'. Reasoning usage is exposed as reasoning_tokens.

release_date.notes: Release notes, July 8 2026: 'Grok 4.5, SpaceXAI's model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, is now available on the xAI API.' A follow-up entry on July 17 2026 records EU console availability.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Not documented. The models page now publishes a cutoff for grok-4.6 only ('The knowledge cut-off date of Grok 4.6 is February 1, 2026'); the grok-4.5 model card states none. Left null rather than inferred.

detail.notes: GA 2026-07-08, superseded five weeks later by grok-4.6 (2026-08-12) but still fully priced, rate-limited and documented — kept in the roster as a live, cheaper-cache alternative at identical headline rates. Aliases per the model card: grok-4.5-latest and grok-build-latest (i.e. grok-4.5 now backs the 'build' alias that previously pointed at grok-build-0.1). Reasoning effort tops out at 'high' (no xhigh). Same 200-tool aggregate per-request cap and the same absence of a batch discount as grok-4.6.

context_window_tokens.notes: Model card: 'Context window: 1,000,000'; pricing table confirms 1M. Still the LARGEST xAI window — larger than both grok-4.6 and grok-4.5 (500k each), which makes grok-4.3 the better host for a big MCP tool surface even though it is no longer the flagship.

input_output_shared.notes: Single published context number; separate input/output pools are not documented. OpenAI-compatible convention implied.

max_input_tokens.notes: No separate max-input cap documented; cannot be derived because no max-output figure is published.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: No default max-output value published on the model card or API reference (re-checked 2026-08-19).

max_output_tokens_max.notes: No maximum single-completion cap published; the 1M shared window is what binds.

extended_context.notes: No extended/beta window beyond 1M. The 200k long-context threshold in pricing is a billing boundary, not a window. The old aggregator claim of a ~2M 'Grok 4 Fast' window remains unconfirmed — grok-4-fast-* were retired on 2026-05-15 and redirected to grok-4.3.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: 'Reasoning tokens: Full completion token price' — reasoning tokens bill at the output rate and are reported via reasoning_tokens in usage. The reasoning docs add: 'reasoning_effort defaults to high. Reasoning cannot be disabled.'

tokenizer_family.notes: xAI still publishes no tokenizer name, no HF tokenizer repo and no tiktoken base. The API reference (re-read 2026-08-19) documents Chat/Images/Videos/Voice/Models/Files/Batches endpoint families and no tokenizer or count-tokens endpoint. 'xai-grok' is a placeholder label, not a vendor-published family name.

tokenizer_public.notes: No public tokenizer library, HF repo or tiktoken base found as of 2026-08-19; no count-tokens endpoint in the API reference. Medium confidence: absence of documentation is not proof of absence.

tokenizer_access.notes: Closed for programmatic local use. The interactive Tokenizer Playground in the xAI console remains the only exploration path; no API and no library are documented.

count_tokens_method.notes: No count-tokens API endpoint documented (unlike OpenAI's token-counting endpoint or Google countTokens). Searched docs.x.ai API reference and the web for an xAI count-tokens endpoint on 2026-08-19 and found none. Local estimation must fall back to the raw_json_rough profile.

image_token_rule.notes: Image input is supported but xAI publishes no image-to-token conversion rule (no tile/patch formula like OpenAI's). Image tokens are billed as input tokens.

audio_token_rule.notes: No audio input on the text models; speech is handled by the separate Voice / Speech-to-Speech API models. No audio token rule applies here.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Set to null on 2026-08-19: xAI publishes no characters-per-token ratio and no tokenizer, and the previously recorded '4' carried no source. Searched docs.x.ai and OpenAI's token-counting guide for a citable rule of thumb and found none applicable to Grok. Use the dataset's raw_json_rough (bytes/4) floor and label it an estimate.

batch_discount.notes: CHANGED 2026-08-19: the pricing page now names the batch-eligible models explicitly — 'grok-4.3, grok-4.20-0309-reasoning, grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning, grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309' at 20% off, text/language models only, and 'Models not listed above have no batch discount.' Confidence lowered from medium to low — the previously cited release-notes evidence no longer states this date.

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Set to null on 2026-08-19. The previously cited sentence ('The knowledge cut-off date of Grok 3 and Grok 4 is November, 2024') is no longer present on the models page, which now documents a cutoff for grok-4.6 only. The grok-4.3 model card states none. Rather than carry a value whose source no longer says it, this is nulled.

detail.notes: Superseded as flagship by grok-4.5 (2026-07-08) and then grok-4.6 (2026-08-12), but still GA: it keeps its own model card, full pricing row, and a Tier 0-4 rate-limit row, with no deprecation banner as of 2026-08-19. Trade-offs vs grok-4.6: lower throughput (37 RPS / 10M TPM vs 150 RPS / 50M TPM at Tier 0), us-east-1 only, and no published knowledge cutoff. Aliases: grok-4.3-latest.

context_window_tokens.notes: Pricing table lists grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309 at 1M context, unchanged.

input_output_shared.notes: Shared pool assumed per OpenAI-compatible convention; not explicitly stated. Note the window applies to the leader agent's context — sub-agents consume their own tokens, all billed.

max_input_tokens.notes: Not documented.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Multi-agent docs (re-read 2026-08-19): 'The max_tokens parameter is not currently supported by the multi-agent model variant.' No default is published and the parameter cannot be set.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: max_tokens is not supported for this variant, so no caller-settable output ceiling exists and none is published.

extended_context.notes: No extended window beyond 1M; the 200k long-context figure is a pricing threshold.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Multi-agent docs: 'All tokens consumed by both the leader agent and sub-agents are billed, including input tokens, output tokens, and reasoning tokens.' reasoning_effort selects agent count (low/medium = 4 agents, high/xhigh = 16), so effort multiplies billed reasoning tokens rather than just deepening one chain.
